name: NoiseSense — Acoustic AI & Real-Time Noise Mapping
tagline: Distributed IoT pipeline classifying 521 sound categories in real time
purpose: Real-time environmental noise monitoring, acoustic event classification, and GPS-tagged noise heatmap generation for smart city infrastructure.
problem_solved: Cities and industrial zones lack real-time acoustic intelligence. Traditional noise monitoring uses manual spot-checks. NoiseSense creates a continuous, distributed, intelligent acoustic monitoring network.

pipeline: YAMNet ML Inference (521 sound category classification)
Gemini AI PDF Report Generation (automated forensic reports)
architecture.description: Asynchronous pub-sub IoT pipeline. Edge devices capture audio, extract DSP features, run YAMNet inference locally, and publish classified events via MQTT to a central broker. InfluxDB stores time-series data with GPS coordinates. Grafana visualizes live heatmaps. Gemini AI generates automated forensic PDF reports on request.
key_design_choices: Edge inference (YAMNet on device) to minimize bandwidth
MQTT pub-sub for sub-50ms event transport
InfluxDB for high-frequency time-series write performance
Offline-first design with 100% recovery on reconnect

key_achievements: 85%+ ML classification accuracy across 521 AudioSet sound categories
Sub-50ms MQTT telemetry latency from capture to broker
GPS-tagged noise heatmaps with real-time Grafana visualization
Automated Gemini AI forensic PDF report generation
100% data recovery after network disconnection events
Fully containerized with Docker Compose for one-command deployment

engineering_decisions.reason: MQTT's pub-sub model gives sub-50ms transport latency versus REST polling overhead. Also designed for IoT constrained devices — low power, low bandwidth. REST would require polling and is not event-driven.

engineering_decisions.decision: Why YAMNet over custom trained model?
engineering_decisions.reason: YAMNet is pre-trained on 521 AudioSet classes by Google. Training a custom model from scratch would require massive labeled acoustic datasets. YAMNet provides state-of-the-art accuracy out-of-the-box with transfer learning capability.

InfluxDB is purpose-built for time-series data. For IoT event streams with timestamps and GPS coordinates, InfluxDB outperforms PostgreSQL by 10x on write throughput and has native time-range query support.

Sending raw audio over network is bandwidth-intensive and creates privacy concerns. Running inference on the edge device sends only structured event data (class, confidence, timestamp, GPS) — dramatically reducing bandwidth.

challenges: Maintaining data integrity when MQTT broker goes offline — solved with offline buffer and guaranteed delivery on reconnect
Reducing YAMNet inference time on CPU-only edge hardware — optimized with audio chunk sizing and batch processing
GPS accuracy in indoor environments — handled with fallback to last known position
